Neither has a "fallback to direct fetch" path in production.

result.plan:
## BD 402 Impact (1 paragraph)

Two production cron-driven scrapers are silently broken. **`duval-clerk-recordings`** (daily 06:00 ET, `lib/scrapers/dispatch/duval-clerk-recordings.ts:61`) hits BD via `PlaywrightSession`, which throws unconditionally on BD edge failure — BullMQ retries 5x with exponential backoff, then marks the job failed, so ~1,078 Duval Clerk recordings/day are not landing. **`realauction-fl-foreclosures`** (every 15 min, 06:00–09:00 ET = 16 runs/morning, `lib/scrapers/dispatch/realauction-fl-foreclosures.ts:38`) loops 16 FL counties × 3 tracks (foreclosure/tax-deed/tax-lien); per-county `try/catch` swallows the BD error, so every run "succeeds" with `rowCount=0`, meaning ~48 county-track slots per morning silently produce no rows. Critically: the audit's INPUT 2 finding flips the diagnosis — **HTTP 402 from BD is *not* billing/quota** (that's 407 for suspension, 502 for quota-exhausted). Per BD's error catalog, 402 means residential-network access restriction on the target host (KYC-gated site, robots.txt, bad_endpoint). So the original "BD billing is broken" framing may be wrong; this could be a zone-product / target-policy issue. Top-5 metro tax-delinquent scrapers (F2.3) and FL DOR NAL/SDF ingest are unaffected — they don't route through BD.

## What `scripts/check-bd-status.ts` should do

**Env vars required:**
- `BRIGHT_DATA_PROXY_URL` (existing) — for live proxied fetch
- `BRIGHT_DATA_API_TOKEN` (new) — bearer token from BD dashboard → Account settings → API token
- `BRIGHT_DATA_ZONE_NAME` (new, optional; defaults to parsing `zone-<name>` out of the proxy URL username)

**What it checks (3 layers, defensive — BD API surface is inconsistently documented, so fall through on 404):**
1. **BD account API** — `GET /status` (account ok + `can_make_requests` + `auth_fail_reason`), `GET /zone/get_active_zones` (assert our zone is listed; absence = disabled/deleted), `GET /zone/status?zone=…` (live state), `GET /zone/bw?zone=…&from=…&to=…` (MTD bytes), `GET /zone?zone=…` (plan cap).
2. **Live proxied fetches against 2 known-good public URLs** — `https://geo.brdtest.com/welcome.txt?country=us` (BD's own health URL) and `https://httpbin.org/ip`. This is the source of truth if the API endpoints drift — captures HTTP status, `x-brd-error`/`x-luminati-error` headers, and `retry-after`.
3. **Live Playwright session test** — same as what `duval-clerk-recordings` actually does, against a trivial target, to confirm the stealth-chromium path works end-to-end (not just plain HTTPS).

**Output:** a single console table — columns: `check | status | detail` — covering account, zone-active, MTD usage / cap %, each live-fetch HTTP code, BD error header, Playwright bootstrap result. Plus a one-line verdict.

**Exit codes:** `0`=healthy, `1`=zone disabled/missing, `2`=quota exhausted (HTTP 502 from proxy OR MTD > cap), `3`=other (auth failed, 407 suspension, network error, unclassified).

**Approach given uncertainty:** BD's docs show inconsistent paths (`/zone` vs `/zone/info` vs `/zone/status`) and per INPUT 2 some endpoints may 404. The script treats the **live proxied fetch as ground truth** — if the stats API is unreachable, it still produces a verdict from the live test. The stats API is "nice to have" for the MTD-usage number; the pass/fail decision can be made from the live fetch alone.

## What I (Claude) will write next

**File:** `flipops-site/scripts/check-bd-status.ts`

Function sketch:
- `parseZoneFromProxyUrl(url)` — extract `zone-<name>` from the username so the script works without `BRIGHT_DATA_ZONE_NAME` set.
- `checkAccountStatus(token)` — hits `/status`; returns `{accountOk, authFailReason}` or `{skipped: true}` on 404.
- `checkZoneActive(token, zone)` — hits `/zone/get_active_zones` + `/zone/status?zone=…`; defensive on 404.
- `checkZoneUsage(token, zone)` — hits `/zone/bw` (UTC ISO `from`=month-start, `to`=now) and `/zone?zone=…`; returns `{mtdBytes, planCap, pctUsed}` or null.
- `liveProxyFetch(proxyUrl, targetUrl)` — uses existing `politeFetch` via `lib/scrapers/base/http-client.ts` with `useProxy:true`; captures `status`, `x-brd-error`, `retry-after`.
- `livePlaywrightTest(proxyUrl)` — spins up a `PlaywrightSession` against `https://geo.brdtest.com/welcome.txt`; confirms stealth-chromium path.
- `renderTable(results)` — plain `console.log` table.
- `main()` — runs all, picks exit code by precedence (zone-disabled > quota > auth > other > ok).

## What I CANNOT do (so the user knows what's still on them)

- **Actual BD dashboard work** — adding a payment method, clearing a negative balance, re-enabling a suspended zone, completing KYC for full residential access, or switching zone product type. All of that is in BD's control panel (`https://brightdata.com/cp/setting/billing` and `…/zones`).
- **Generating the `BRIGHT_DATA_API_TOKEN`** — you have to copy it from BD → Account settings → API token and paste into `.env.local`. I can't read it from the dashboard.
- **Confirming the *real* root cause** is billing vs. residential-policy until either (a) the script runs against a working token, or (b) a fresh 402 is captured with `response.headers` + body persisted to `scripts/probe-artifacts/` (the audit found zero existing BD-402 artifacts — the original 402 was never captured).
- **Re-classifying the in-app alerts** that currently say "BD billing" — that's a follow-up edit to scraper-layer error handling once we know it's actually 407/502.

## Recommended next step after BD is restored

Re-run `npx tsx scripts/check-bd-status.ts` to confirm exit code 0, then we resume the deferred Option B v0 build (or pivot to capturing+persisting raw BD error headers in `scripts/probe-artifacts/` so the next outage isn't a guessing game).
